chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

'There is nothing between you and those who oppose you except the al-Matmar.' I said: 'And what is the al-Matmar?' He said: 'That which you call al-Tar (the plumb line). So whoever opposes you and crosses it, then dissociate from him, even if he is an Alawite and Fatimid.'

key_terms.ابْرَؤُوا: Dissociate; to declare innocence or separation from someone.
key_terms.التَّرَّ: The plumb; a tool used to determine verticality, here used metaphorically for the line of separation.
key_terms.الْمَطْمَرُ: The plumb line; a boundary or line of demarcation.
key_terms.عَلَوِيًّا: Alawite; a descendant of Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.فَاطِمِيًّا: Fatimid; a descendant of Fatimah (peace be upon her).

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'plumb line' (al-Matmar) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defining *al-Matmar* (the plumb line) as the decisive criterion for *bara'ah* (dissociation) from opponents, emphasizing that this boundary is based on adherence to the truth rather than mere genealogy. This concept underscores the Shia principle that even a descendant of the Prophet (Fatimi) is subject to separation if they deviate from the established path of the Imams, highlighting the supremacy of doctrinal fidelity over lineage. The 'plumb line' serves as a metaphor for the straight, upright path of the Ahl al-Bayt, against which all claims are measured.
